name: FL-17
label: Likely R

key_factors: District leans Republican by about ten points and the incumbent is running
Steube holds roughly a 20-to-1 cash advantage over his Democratic challenger
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 95%
No public polls or expert ratings, so uncertainty rests on structural signals
model.rationale: The district's ten-point Republican lean, Steube's overwhelming financial edge, and markets pricing his win near 95% leave little evidence of a competitive race; the forecast rests on district lean, money, and market pricing, with a wide uncertainty band because no polls are available.
model.watch: Any late polling, outside spending, or fundraising surge by Montavon signaling unexpected competitiveness would warrant a shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Florida's 17th District leans Republican by about ten points, and Republican Greg Steube is seeking re-election with the advantages of incumbency. He has raised roughly $1.3 million and holds about $2.1 million in cash, while Democratic challenger Matthew Montavon has raised under $100,000 with about $24,000 available. An independent, Michael Quirk, is also on the ballot with minimal funding. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets put the Republican's chances around 95%.

The combination of a favorable district, a well-funded incumbent, and an under-resourced challenger makes a Democratic upset hard to see. The forecast expects Steube to win by a comfortable double-digit margin, with uncertainty wide enough to reflect the absence of polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
